transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-05
Start time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Carlos Rivera (Aegis DevOps), Priya Nair (Aegis Platform Eng), Tom Holden (Aegis Security), Mei Zhang (Aegis ML Infra), Justin (Aegis SRE)

Summary (auto): weekly POC checkpoint for Redwood Private on VPC-connected on-prem pilot. Reviewed this week's benchmark results after kernel/quantization tweaks, discussed a recurring routing flap causing 503s, confirmed required network changes (peering and NAT), agreed on a low-risk kernel rollout window, and captured next steps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, thanks everyone for joining. I see most folks are here, we'll aim for about 45 minutes. Quick roll call - Maya (Redwood), Samir (SE), Lena (CSM) - and on the Aegis side?
[00:12] Carlos Rivera: Carlos here, Priya, Tom, Mei and Justin on this call as well.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Perfect. Quick agenda: 1) results from the last tweak (kernel + quantization change), 2) the intermittent routing issue Justin flagged, 3) network changes needed for peering and NAT, and 4) next steps. Samir, you want to start with perf notes?
[00:31] Samir Patel: Yeah sure. So we rolled the 2.1 kernel optimization on Tuesday night to the pilot cluster — this included a slightly different attention kernel and an updated fp16 fallback path for one of the layers. We also adjusted the quantization profile for the 8-bit int path, mainly to avoid a small accuracy drift we saw in the first run.
[00:52] Mei Zhang: Quick q — did you keep the KV cache change we talked about or revert? The KV cache clipping had looked promising for prefix heavy workloads.
[01:03] Samir Patel: We left the KV cache change in but lowered the aggressive expiry threshold. That preserved most hit rate while preventing cache thrash in short-lived sessions.
[01:15] Priya Nair: From our side we ran the nightly load run — 10k synthetic requests with our typical prompt mix. Overall p50 dropped by about 12%, p95 by 18%, p99 about 9% — CPU on the control plane agent was lower too. But we still saw a spike of 503s around 03:00 UTC.
[01:39] Justin (SRE): Yep that spike is what I'm worried about. It looks like a routing flap between the customer VPC and the on-prem NAT gateway — not sure if it's a BGP withdraw or a transient MTU issue. The SRE logs show timeouts at the egress for ~30 seconds.
[01:56] Tom Holden: Security side — that 503 window also correlates with failed audit log uploads to our SIEM. If logs are missing we can't prove compliance for that window. We need a mitigation that keeps logs buffered locally until connectivity is back.
[02:10] Lena Ortiz: Good call — buffering is doable, Samir can you speak to local buffering in the agent?
[02:18] Samir Patel: The private control plane agent can spool logs to disk and retry with exponential backoff; that's already in the agent but the default spool size is small. We can bump spool to 1GB for the pilot cluster; need an OK on disk usage from Aegis.
[02:32] Carlos Rivera: We can allocate extra disk on the pilot nodes, 1GB is fine. But the bigger concern is the root cause for the network flap. Justin says it could be BGP-related — are we peering through a transit gateway?
[02:47] Justin (SRE): We're peering via the cloud transit gateway and then an on-prem BGP session to our edge. The timing shows the transit gateway replaced a route on a health check failure; that coincided with a connection drain on the Redwood agent.
[03:02] Maya Chen: Okay, two actionable threads: 1) make logs resilient, bump spool, 2) root cause network flap. Samir, you mentioned kernel rollout — what's the expected downtime and risk?
[03:14] Samir Patel: The kernel patch is rolling as a rolling restart with no required model reload in theory, but in practice each worker restarts and reconnects to the gRPC frontends. We recommend a 15–30 minute maintenance window to observe drains and fallbacks; there might be a small p95 blip during the window. We have a canary group in the cluster so we can stage it to 10% first.
[03:37] Priya Nair: We need to coordinate with our change window — next Thursday night is preferred for us 02:00–03:00 local. Is that compatible with your canary plan?
[03:46] Samir Patel: That works. We'll do 10% canary for 20 minutes, monitor errors and latency, then ramp. If errors exceed threshold we'll auto rollback.
[03:56] Mei Zhang: On the accuracy side, did the quantization change trigger any regression? Our eval suite flagged a 0.6% drop in one of the sensitive prompt categories.
[04:08] Samir Patel: Good catch. The 0.6% was within expectations but we can push a tweak: slightly increase per-channel scale for that layer to reduce the bias. That will cost ~2% more perf at the microkernel level but should restore accuracy.
[04:26] Carlos Rivera: We'd prefer accuracy >99.5% on the eval set for that category. If the tweak does it, go ahead; just document the expected perf delta.
[04:35] Samir Patel: Will do.
[04:38] [05:00] (background) Unknown Speaker: um hmm
[05:02] Justin (SRE): Returning to routing, one pattern — when our primary transit health-check fails it fails a handful of connections and the transit gateway switches to backup path that passes through a different edge with an MTU 1400 vs our usual 1500. That causes path MTU discovery issues and fragmentation leading to gRPC stalls.
[05:25] Maya Chen: Interesting, so it may be an MTU drop causing gRPC stalls which surface as 503?
[05:31] Samir Patel: gRPC is sensitive to path MTU, yeah. If packets are fragmented and the agent doesn't handle sticky sessions at the application layer, the connection can reset. A quick mitigation is to enable MSS clamping or ensure tunnel path MTU is consistent.
[05:44] Priya Nair: We can set MSS clamp on the edge devices but that requires a config change and a short window. Justin, can you coordinate with network ops?
[05:52] Justin (SRE): Yep I'll open a ticket right after this call. Also recommend Redwood add a client-side keepalive and slightly longer gRPC retry before surfacing 503 to the app.
[06:03] Samir Patel: We can bump the keepalive interval and retries in the agent; that'll reduce transient 503s from short flaps. We'll push a config that doesn't need a full agent restart.
[06:12] Tom Holden: From compliance, we still need to ensure audit logs are marked as 'delayed' with a clear chain of custody when buffering happens. Will Redwood provide log checksums on upload?
[06:24] Samir Patel: Yes, logs are hashed and we support upload with a manifest that includes SHA256. When we spool and then push we include the manifest so you can verify integrity.
[06:35] Mei Zhang: On perf numbers, can you show the raw latency histograms again? The dashboard snapshot we looked at showed mean 80ms down to 70ms but p99 is still kinda noisy.
[06:48] Maya Chen: Lena, can you drop that dashboard link in the notes?
[06:52] Lena Ortiz: Sure — sending now in the chat — "link: pilot-cluster-dashboard/aegis-0305"
[07:00] [07:15] Maya Chen: Great. Let's pivot to routing fixes and peering planning — Carlos, you mentioned CIDR overlaps earlier?
[07:22] Carlos Rivera: Right, our staging VPC uses 10.0.0.0/16 and our pilot VPC is 10.1.0.0/16, transit is 10.255.0.0/16 but the on-prem uses 10.0.0.0/14 for historical reasons. That overlap could cause unexpected route preference during failover. We need to confirm no overlapping prefixes are installed to the transit.
[07:45] Mei Zhang: That could explain why the transit sometimes picks a path that routes internal traffic back to the wrong edge.
[07:52] Priya Nair: We can carve out a dedicated /20 for the Redwood peering to avoid overlap. It's low touch but requires change control.
[07:59] Maya Chen: Redwood requires that the peering prefix not overlap with any customer internal prefixes; if you can confirm a /20 that is unused we can provision the VPC peering and NAT rules. Also note we need route propagation disabled for that peering to avoid accidental export.
[08:18] Carlos Rivera: I'll check and propose a /20 by Monday.
[08:21] Justin (SRE): Also check egress NAT gateway limits — during the benchmark we spiked and the NAT threw connection limits causing some resets. We might need multiple NAT gateways or a higher throughput tier.
[08:34] Maya Chen: Good call. For pilot, dual NAT or a single HA NAT is recommended. We'll document the recommended network topology in the follow-up.
[08:41] [09:00] (typing) Lena Ortiz: dropping network topo doc link: "docs/aegis-network-topo-v1"
[09:08] Priya Nair: On encryption and KMS — Tom — any new asks?
[09:12] Tom Holden: We want to ensure CMKs are customer-managed for Private. If keys are rotated we need a pre-signed key rotation plan and notice. Also need proof of HSM-backed keys if possible for later compliance.
[09:25] Samir Patel: Redwood private supports BYOK via KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed providers. We'll attach the KM integration guide in the follow-up.
[09:34] Tom Holden: Also need proof of SOC2 controls around key access, can you share that doc?
[09:39] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send the SOC2 control mapping for Private deployments. Lena will attach in the follow-up.
[09:46] Mei Zhang: Another smaller item — model pinning behavior during canary rollouts. If we can pin a model SHA to canary nodes it would help reproducibility. Are rollouts model-aware?
[09:58] Samir Patel: Yes, rollouts can be model-version-aware. We do canary groups by node label and model-version pinning. We'll provide the rollout recipe we plan to use for the 2.1 kernel canary.
[10:10] Maya Chen: Good. Let's capture the agreed maintenance window: Thursday 02:00–03:00 local for Aegis, Redwood to start 10% canary at 02:05, monitor 20 minutes then ramp. If errors >1% we roll back. Samir, confirm?
[10:24] Samir Patel: Confirmed. We'll provide a runbook and the rollback metric thresholds.
[10:29] [10:45] Justin (SRE): On the quick term routing mitigation, I'll set MSS clamp on the edge and increase health-check timeout to reduce false failovers. That should reduce flaps.
[10:57] Carlos Rivera: We'll also provision the extra disk for spool and validate that agents pick up new spool size without restart.
[11:07] Mei Zhang: After the kernel roll, can we run a focused bench for our heavy-prefix prompts and then reconvene? I want a p95/p99 comparison within 48 hours of the rollout.
[11:18] Lena Ortiz: I'll schedule a benchmark run and a follow-up 48-hour sync.
[11:23] Maya Chen: Awesome. Any other blockers?
[11:26] Priya Nair: One ask — can Redwood provide a short note on the expected perf delta if we revert the KV cache expiry tweak? We want to know risk surface if we need to rollback fast.
[11:37] Samir Patel: I'll include a revert impact note in the runbook — expected p50 up by ~8% if we revert, and p95 may go back to previous levels.
[11:47] [12:00] (short crosstalk; someone says thanks)
[12:03] Maya Chen: All right, quick recap — Samir will share kernel changelog/runbook + revert impact + log spool config by 2025-03-06; Carlos will confirm /20 for peering and NAT capacity by 2025-03-10; Mei will provide payloads and latency targets by 2025-03-09; Lena will schedule the benchmark and send SOC2/key docs. Redwood and Aegis agree on timeline and Thursday night canary.
[12:25] Maya Chen: Any objections?
[12:28] Tom Holden: No objections. Just need the audit log manifest and SOC2 mapping.
[12:33] Maya Chen: We'll include those. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and in the shared docs.
[12:40] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional misattributions and background speech; some technical acronyms mistranscribed (e.g., MSS clamping written as "M S S clamp" in original auto text).
